references.text: The servant bows down and worships the Lord (same word pair: קדד and שׁחה) and blesses God for His faithfulness and guidance - exactly the same action he recounts in verse 48.
The servant's original prayer to God for guidance, which he now recounts to Rebekah's family in verse 48 along with the result: God led him on the right path.
The people bowed down and worshipped (וַיִּקֹּד הָעָם וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲוּ) - the same word pair as in Gen 24:48, expressing gratitude and worship toward the Lord.
The call to bow down and worship the Lord mirrors the servant's action in Gen 24:48 where he bowed and worshipped.
'Acknowledge him in all your ways, and he will make your paths straight' - a parallel to the servant's experience of the Lord leading him on the right path (דרך אמת).
'Blessed be God, the Most High' - Abraham blesses God after victory, just as the servant blesses the Lord after being led on the right way.
Complementary parts of the same prayer and expression of gratitude in the servant's travel account.
The prayer for guidance (v.12) and the confirmation that the guidance has been completed (v.48).
The introduction and conclusion of the same prayer at the well.
The fulfillment of Abraham's promise of descendants and blessing in Isaac's time.
A parallel in prayer for God's guidance connected to Abraham's promise and lineage.
Abraham's faith in God's promise (v.7) and the servant's confirmation that the promise is fulfilled (v.48).
Contrast between true divine guidance (v.48) and human manipulation using the same wording (v.27:20).
A parallel in praise for God's fulfillment of promises.
A parallel in praise for God's fulfillment of promises.
A parallel in God's guidance and protection of Abraham's descendants during their journey.
The oath (v.23) and the confirmation of God's guidance (v.48) in the same story.
Worship before (v.26) and after (v.48) God's action in the same story.
A parallel in God's guidance and protection of Abraham's offspring throughout their lives.
